**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the concentration curve in the version gate**

When `CONCENTRATION_FORMULA_VERSION` moves before its pairing is admitted and the package contains a retained curve, this branch skips `concentration.derive`, but `_analysed` still unconditionally appends `_curve_figures(package)` after the loop. `curve_series` stamps the moved family version, and `_section` treats those figures as a present concentration section and discards the recorded refusal. The rollout window this gate targets therefore still publishes concentration output under an unadmitted pairing; gate curve creation with the rest of the concentration family and test that mismatch explicitly.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L16-L16](https://github.com/Kemetra/Khepri/blob/70369d4343d45776e5d8e7536102717672449323/AGENTS.md#L16-L16)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Identify the refused family in the customer message**

When any family hits this version refusal, the Excel limitations sheet writes only this message, without the section heading (`excel.py` lines 660–667). Because all four families share the code, “This analysis” does not tell the customer whether comparison, concentration, growth, or basket analysis is unavailable, and multiple mismatches produce indistinguishable entries. This conflicts with RRA-009's requirement that each refusal name the unavailable business capability; include the section-specific business name in the rendered message.
